title: A closed capped corridor is a disconnection, not a distance
statement: If breadth-first search over presentations of total relator length at most the cap exhausts its frontier from the start without reaching the target, and the target lies inside the cap, then the start and the target lie in different connected components of the length-capped move graph. For every official AC row the target has length 2 and every cap is at least 9, so every exhausted corridor is such a disconnection.
assumptions: The move set and cancellation rule of the official verifier; the cap applied to total relator length; exhaustive enumeration of the start's component within the cap.
failure_mode: Component size says nothing about whether the target is in that component, so a large corridor does not make a certificate likely. A cap proof excludes only paths inside the cap. The closed-set bottleneck method itself is not novel; the candidate contribution is the reproducible instance table on hard official rows.
evidence_status: Exact finite computation with the official verifier: six pairwise-disjoint components and twelve closed corridors on the complete length-39 profile (15 September 2026). A target-outside Lean barrier theorem exists on PR #69 (draft); its numerical rows are release-gate pending.
verification_scope: claude/confident-fermi-09rd02 commits b8ec58b5, 452ead28, ec60f90e, 0eedd1fb, e56bd253; tools/acc/ATLAS_TRANSFER_TRANSPORT_v1.md section 1; ACCSublevelBarrier.lean on proof/acc-sublevel-barriers-2026-09-19 at 471cdc6f84c6b1b9702ead754106de94a36c3264.

title: Identical reduced observations can conceal opposite response slopes
statement: A specified two-orbital pair has equal initial conductance and equal isolated optical transition strength, yet has distinct displaced transmissions and opposite local response directions. For the joint record R(s)=(T_s(0), 1/(s^2+4)), R(+1)=R(-1)=(1/2,1/5) while T_+(1/10)=8100/19981 and T_-(1/10)=12100/20021; their exact separation is 79600000/400039601. No deterministic function of the joint record predicts both later values, and any single prediction assigned to that record has worst-case absolute error at least half the separation.
assumptions: Fixed two-orbital Hamiltonian family, wide-band contacts, physical reference basis, noninteracting coherent scattering and the declared isolated optical probe. The robustness theorem uses independent absolute response errors bounded by 1/20 per model.
failure_mode: A reduced snapshot can be exact and still be non-identifying. Additional coordinates help only if they carry information not already factored out by the observation map. Arbitrary future response cannot be reconstructed from one boundary snapshot without a model.
evidence_status: Revision-4 finite theorem/certificate result; joint-record equality, no-predictor theorem, exact separation, minimax lower bound and robustness margin compile in Lean/mathlib on PR #25 (LC-012)
verification_scope: Certified source commit 6955e481b15b25bb2a615a93f27573713adcfcea, GitHub Actions run 34691594067, Lean 4.33.0 / Mathlib db584cd6; leanchecker and axiom audit passed. The pinned path below is at the PR #25 head 7e9f1ddc, which postdates the certified commit. Finite model mathematics, not a universal physical prediction theorem.
credit: Classical Feshbach, Fano and graph-projector identities; Beasley source manuscripts supply the observation architecture. The Revision-4 contribution sharpens the benchmark into an exact joint-record minimax obstruction with formal certificates.
next_step: Calibrated held-out physical prediction with recorded geometry, phase reference, intervention and denominator-bearing boundary labels.
